claim_verdicts.evidence: Definition of the vocab term; matches content/glossary.yaml cache-invalidation short_en "Removing a cached copy when the source data changes, so the next read gets the new value". Definitional, no external source needed.

Round 1 lab run 2026-09-28: `redis-cli MONITOR` during the staff PATCH /api/v1/products/3 (StackExchange.Redis 3.3.1 -> redis 8.10.2) recorded `"UNLINK" "product:3"` from the api, no DEL. SE.Redis release notes 2.0.571: "Fix: KeyDeleteAsync could, in some cases, always use DEL (instead of UNLINK)". Redis UNLINK docs: "very similar to DEL: it removes the specified keys". Lesson section 3 now says only "asks Redis to delete a key and its value", which holds for both.

Claim now scoped to Đơn Hàng as suggested in round 1. `git grep` at stage-2: product:{id} is written only by ProductCache.SetAsync (StringSetAsync with Ttl) and removed only by ProductCache.RemoveAsync (KeyDeleteAsync). Eviction does not apply in the lab: round 1 `CONFIG GET maxmemory` -> 0 ("Set maxmemory to zero to specify that you don't want to limit the memory"). Nothing in the repo links Redis to PostgreSQL.

stage-2 ProductsController.cs:63-70: `[Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")] [HttpPatch("{id:int}")] public async Task<ActionResult<ProductDto>> UpdatePrice(int id, UpdateProductPriceRequest request) { var product = await products.UpdatePriceAsync(id, request.PriceVnd); if (product is null) return NotFound(); return Ok(new ProductDto(...)); }`; route prefix `[Route("api/v1/products")]` line 14.
stage-2 ProductCache.cs:54-58: `var product = await inner.UpdatePriceAsync(id, priceVnd); if (product is not null) await RemoveAsync($"product:{id}"); return product;`

stage-2 EfProductRepository.cs:11-18: `var product = await db.Products.FindAsync(id); if (product is null) return null; product.PriceVnd = priceVnd; await db.SaveChangesAsync(); return product;`. ProductCache.cs:56 awaits it with no try/catch, so an exception from SaveChangesAsync propagates before line 57 (RemoveAsync) runs.

Code inspection, stage-2 ProductCache.cs:28-43: miss -> lock -> second GetAsync miss -> `inner.FindAsync(id)` (old row, save not yet done) -> `SetAsync(key, product)` which calls `StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl)` (line 83), Ttl = 5 min (line 18). Comment lines 52-53 states the same.

ProductCache.cs @ stage-2: the old-price read must reach `inner.FindAsync` (line 41), i.e. both GetAsync calls (28, 38) missed, so the key had to be absent — the added condition is correct. UpdatePriceAsync (54-59) never takes `Locks` (only FindAsync, 33-48), so its RemoveAsync can run between that read's FindAsync and SetAsync. Redis SET docs: "The key is created if it doesn't exist." SetAsync writes with Ttl (83), so the copy lives until the TTL ends.

stage-2 ProductCache.cs:16-18: `// The longest a stale copy can live, even if a delete below is missed.` `private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);`; line 83 `StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl)` is the only write.

Lab run 2026-09-28, redis container stopped, staff PATCH /api/v1/products/3 {priceVnd:890000} -> `-> 200`. api log: `"Message":"Redis delete of product:3 failed; the old copy lives until its TTL ends","Exception":"StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException: No connection is active/available ...` then `PATCH /api/v1/products/3 responded 200`. Code ProductCache.cs:91-101 catches `RedisException or RedisTimeoutException`, no rethrow. Redis restarted, price unchanged.
claim_verdicts.source: lab run: docker compose stop redis + curl PATCH + docker compose logs api; ProductCache.cs:91-101 @ stage-2

claim_verdicts.evidence: `git grep KeyDelete stage-2` -> only ProductCache.cs:95 (RemoveAsync), called only from UpdatePriceAsync (57). A psql UPDATE bypasses it, so product:{id} stays until the Ttl set in SetAsync. PostgreSQL 17 psql page: "psql is a terminal-based front-end to PostgreSQL. It enables you to type in queries interactively, issue them to PostgreSQL, and see the query results." — matches "PostgreSQL's command-line client".
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: git grep KeyDelete / RemoveAsync; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/app-psql.html

Redis EXISTS docs: "Returns the number of keys that exist." Return: "Integer reply: the number of keys that exist from those specified as arguments." Examples: `EXISTS key1` -> 1, `EXISTS nosuchkey` -> 0.

issues.text: Misconception 3 says the delete-first gap shows "only when many customers" read around the PATCH. One read landing between the delete and the save is enough (section 4 paragraph 3 and quiz q3 use a single customer); many readers only make it likely. "only when many" states a condition the code does not require.
issues.quote: You notice this only when many customers open product 3 around the moment of the `PATCH`
issues.fix: "You notice this when a customer opens product 3 between the delete and the save, which is likely when many customers open it around the moment of the `PATCH`: they see the old price although the `PATCH` answered `200` with the new one."

issues.text: Summary line 1 says "when a price changes, ProductCache deletes the cached copy"; section 5 (and quiz q5) establish that a price changed with psql deletes nothing. The line was scoped to Đơn Hàng after round 1 (partly this reviewer's own suggested text) but still covers all price changes.
issues.quote: In Đơn Hàng, when a price changes, `ProductCache` deletes the cached copy right after the database save
issues.fix: "In Đơn Hàng, when staff change a price through the API, `ProductCache` deletes the cached copy right after the database save, so the next read loads the new price."

issues.text: The explanation for d states a rule the lesson never gives ("deletes a key whether or not it has a TTL") and backs it with the script, but in the script product:3 was stored with a 5-minute TTL, so EXISTS printing 0 does not show a key without TTL can be deleted. I can still reject d, but the evidence confuses me.
issues.quote: Redis deletes a key whether or not it has a TTL; the script's `EXISTS product:3` printing `0` shows the delete works.
issues.fix: Drop the script evidence and point to section 3: "`KeyDeleteAsync` deletes a key and its value; nothing in the lesson ties deleting to a TTL. The reason to keep the TTL is missed deletes, not the delete itself."
